technical_and_design_decisions: For Kafka and Rabbit test rule extraction (U1, U2): New dedicated repositories will use Maven matching the core SCDF project's build tool, with versioned releases published to the internal artifact registry, and backward-compatible APIs for existing test fixtures to avoid breaking changes in dependent projects.

For cross-platform consistent REST APIs (U3): A unified REST controller layer will be implemented on top of existing platform-specific service implementations, using a platform detection service to route requests, without modifying the underlying platform-specific code to minimize implementation risk.

For library artifact registration (U4): Library artifacts will be stored in the existing artifact registry with a new 'type' field set to 'library', with validation enforced at both the API and DSL layers to prevent invalid usage of library artifacts as standalone modules.

For named channels (U5): Named channels will be implemented as a new module type in the Spring Cloud Stream DSL, with validation to prevent source/sink bindings, and support for connecting to other modules via the existing channel binding mechanism.

For StreamController test coverage (U6): Tests will use JUnit 5 and Mockito for unit tests, and Spring Cloud Contract for OpenAPI contract tests, with all tests integrated into the existing CI pipeline to run on every build.

For duplicate stream name prevention (U7): A unique database constraint will be added to the stream name column, with application-level validation to provide user-friendly error messages before attempting database insertion to reduce unnecessary database errors.

For Kinesis source module (U8): The Kinesis source binder will follow the existing Spring Cloud Stream binder pattern, using the AWS Kinesis SDK for Java v2, with configuration properties aligned with other Spring Cloud Stream source binders for consistency and ease of use.
assumptions: The core SCDF, Spring Cloud Stream Kafka/Rabbit binder, and platform-specific (Lattice/YARN/Cloud Foundry) codebases are fully accessible to the development team, with necessary permissions to modify code and publish new artifacts to internal registries.

Existing platform-specific service implementations for Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry are stable and have well-defined, documented APIs that can be wrapped by the unified REST layer without modification to underlying platform code.
The existing artifact registry database schema can be extended to add a 'type' field for artifacts without requiring a data migration for existing non-library artifacts, and without downtime.
The up-to-date OpenAPI specification for all StreamController REST endpoints is available and approved for use in contract testing.
All required test environments (Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS Kinesis, Lattice, YARN, Cloud Foundry) are available and properly configured for development, unit, and integration testing.
AWS Kinesis SDK for Java v2 is already included in the project's dependency management, so no new external dependency approval processes are required.

Code review, merge, and release processes are handled by separate teams, so the estimated effort only includes development, unit testing, and integration testing work, not review cycles or release coordination.

activities.activity_name: Extract Kafka test rule to separate repository
activities.activity_description: Move existing Kafka {{@Rule}} test fixtures from the core SCDF test codebase to a new dedicated Maven repository, configure the build and CI pipeline for the new repo, update all cross-references in existing SCDF modules, publish the first stable version to the internal artifact registry, and add usage documentation for external projects.

activities.activity_name: Extract Rabbit test rule to separate repository
activities.activity_description: Move existing Rabbit {{@Rule}} test fixtures from the core SCDF test codebase to a new dedicated Maven repository, configure the build and CI pipeline for the new repo, update all cross-references in existing SCDF modules, publish the first stable version to the internal artifact registry, and add usage documentation for external projects.

activities.activity_name: Design unified cross-platform REST API abstraction
activities.activity_description: Define common REST endpoint contracts for stream and app management across Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry platforms, map platform-specific implementation differences, and design the abstraction layer to route requests to the correct platform-specific service without modifying underlying platform code.

activities.activity_name: Implement unified REST controller and platform routing
activities.activity_description: Implement the common REST controllers, platform detection service, and request routing logic that delegates to existing platform-specific service implementations, add error handling for unsupported platform operations, and ensure consistent response formats across all platforms.

activities.activity_name: Develop cross-platform REST API integration tests
activities.activity_description: Write integration tests that verify the unified REST endpoints work correctly against mock implementations of Lattice, YARN, and CF platform services, cover all supported operations, error cases, and response format consistency.

activities.activity_name: Extend artifact registry to support library artifacts
activities.activity_description: Modify the existing artifact registry data model and database schema to add a 'type' field for artifacts, update the service layer to support library artifact registration and querying, and modify the artifact registration REST API to accept library type designation.

Add validation logic to the stream definition DSL and REST API to ensure library artifacts are only referenced in include/exclude statements, prevent library artifacts from being used as standalone source/sink/processor modules, and return clear error messages for invalid references.

activities.activity_name: Add named-channel module type to stream DSL
activities.activity_description: Extend the stream definition DSL to support a new 'named-channel' module type, add validation to ensure named channels cannot have source/sink bindings, and update the stream deployment logic to handle named channel modules correctly.

activities.activity_name: Update REST API and validation for named channels
activities.activity_description: Update stream creation and update REST endpoints to accept named-channel module definitions, add input validation for named channel properties, and update any relevant client-side validation rules to support the new module type.

activities.activity_name: Write unit tests for StreamController endpoints
activities.activity_description: Write JUnit 5 unit tests for all StreamController REST endpoints, covering happy path scenarios, input validation errors, authentication/authorization failures, and edge cases, using Mockito to mock service layer dependencies.

activities.activity_name: Implement OpenAPI contract tests for StreamController
activities.activity_description: Implement OpenAPI contract tests using Spring Cloud Contract to verify that StreamController endpoints adhere to the defined OpenAPI specification, integrate contract tests into the existing CI pipeline to run on every build.

Add a unique database constraint on the stream name column in the stream registry, implement application-level validation to check for duplicate names during stream creation and update, and return 409 Conflict responses with clear error messages for duplicate name attempts.

Develop a new Spring Cloud Stream binder module for AWS Kinesis as a source, implement configuration properties for Kinesis stream name, AWS region, credentials, and consumption mode, add support for record deserialization, error handling, and offset management, and write unit and integration tests for the binder.

Run end-to-end tests in a shared test environment to verify all new features (separate test repos, unified REST APIs, library artifacts, named channels, duplicate name prevention, Kinesis module) work correctly together, fix any integration issues or conflicts found.

activities.activity_name: Write documentation for all new features
activities.activity_description: Create user and developer documentation for all delivered capabilities, including usage examples for the separate Kafka/Rabbit test repos, unified cross-platform REST APIs, library artifact registration, named channels, and the Kinesis source module, plus migration guides for breaking changes where applicable.
